solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mrs Mop reported getting hiring for holiday home

indicators.note: reported means the pieces are taken as heard, spoken rather than written

parts.note: Mrs Mop is a jokey British name for a cleaning lady, a char; said aloud it matches CHA
letting out a property is hiring it out, so hiring gives LET

explanation.surface: A cleaner says she has found someone to rent the holiday cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: A char (charwoman) is a British cleaner; 'reported' gives CHA by sound, and LET is hiring out a property.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is a wooden cabin often used as accommodation for vacations, especially in the mountains.

clue.text: Minim or te cryptically

definitions.meaning: a musical note held for two beats, so named in US usage
the two letters T and E make up one of two halves of the word note

explanation.surface: A musical query: minim or te?
explanation.walkthrough: TE is the second half of NOTE, so read cryptically it is half a note.
explanation.definitionFit: American musicians call the minim a half note; and two of the four letters of note are half of it.

clue.text: Vassal's right to include close relative leaving the Navy

indicators.note: to include means one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property against a debt

indicators.note: leaving means letters go out of the word

parts.note: a cousin german is a first cousin, so german means closely related
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A servant's entitlement covers a near kinsman who has quit the fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cousin german' means first cousin, so german is a close relative; 'leaving' removes the scattered R and N, leaving GEMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A liegeman was a feudal subordinate owing service to a lord, just like a vassal.

clue.text: Hilton employed art to embellish sporting contest

indicators.note: to embellish means the letters are dressed up into a new form

explanation.surface: A hotel uses artwork to decorate for a sporting event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to embellish' rearranges HILTON and ART together.
explanation.definitionFit: A triathlon is an endurance race combining swimming, cycling and running.

clue.text: Vandal put in gaol converted into charnel house

indicators.note: put in means one piece is placed inside the other before the shuffle
converted means the combined letters are changed into a new arrangement

parts.note: the Vandals and Goths were both barbarian tribes, so a vandal can be a GOTH

explanation.surface: A vandal is locked in prison, which is then turned into a burial house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vandal' looks like any hooligan, but here it is a tribesman, hence a Goth.
explanation.definitionFit: Golgotha, the place of skulls, is used figuratively for a burial place or ossuary.

clue.text: Meeting of top brass

parts.note: read literally, a gathering of generals, the military top brass

explanation.surface: A gathering of senior officers.
explanation.definitionFit: A general assembly is a full deliberative body, like that of the UN or a church.

clue.text: Allure that starts to generate Lothario's love affair

indicators.note: starts to takes the opening letter of each of the next words

parts.note: an amour is a love affair, from French

explanation.surface: Charm that kicks off a womaniser's romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamour is attractive, exciting charm, which is what allure means.

clue.text: Aircraft trades pounds for a drop of Texaco's aviation fuel

indicators.note: trades means one letter is swapped out for another

parts.note: a triplane is an aircraft with three wings
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from libra

indicators.note: a drop of takes just a little, the first letter

explanation.surface: An aeroplane swaps cash for a little fuel from a petrol company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trades ... for' swaps the L in TRIPLANE for T.
explanation.definitionFit: Triptane is a high-octane hydrocarbon used to boost aircraft fuels.

clue.text: Unnatural sailor's sin with worker

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
to err is to sin
the worker ant is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: A seaman's unnatural sin committed with a labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberrant means departing from the normal course, hence abnormal.

clue.text: North African ordered new regalia

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put into a fresh sequence

explanation.surface: Someone from North Africa commissions a fresh set of royal insignia.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Algeria is a person from North Africa.

clue.text: A tribe moving heavy spar

indicators.note: moving means the letters of the phrase shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A tribe relocating, carrying a heavy pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spar' here is a mineral, not a pole: heavy spar is the old name for barium sulphate.
explanation.definitionFit: Barite is the mineral barium sulphate, traditionally known to miners as heavy spar.

clue.text: Forebear — found no traces

indicators.note: found as in casting metal: the letters are melted down and recast in a new shape

explanation.surface: Genealogical research into a forebear turned up nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' looks like past tense of find, but is the verb to found (cast) used as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a person from whom one is descended, earlier in the family line.

clue.text: Bill for one sending letters

definitions.meaning: a bill is a printed notice stuck up on a wall, a placard
someone who mails things, in a cryptic reading of the word

explanation.surface: A bill presented to someone who sends letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is a placard advertisement, and one who posts mail is literally a poster.

clue.text: Indistinct call by humorist giving signal to resume activities

indicators.note: indistinct means the word is blurred, its letters jumbled

parts.note: Edward Lear was a Victorian humorist famous for nonsense verse

explanation.surface: A comedian's mumbled shout gives the go-ahead to carry on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indistinct' scrambles CALL into ALLC, followed by LEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: After an air raid the siren sounding the danger over let people return to normal business.

clue.text: Inflammation irritates badly

indicators.note: badly means the letters are put together wrongly

explanation.surface: An inflammation that annoys a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Arteritis is inflammation of the walls of the arteries.

clue.text: Irish lad's tonsured, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: tonsured means having the head shaved, i.e. shorn

explanation.surface: An Irish boy has had his head shaved, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: The Irish name is pronounced 'Shawn', matching SHORN in non-rhotic speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Sean is a common Irish boy's name, the Gaelic form of John.

clue.text: Stop in sound by headland for picture of it

indicators.note: in sound means the word is used for how it is pronounced

parts.note: to cease is to stop
a cape is a headland

explanation.surface: A halt in a stretch of water near a promontory, painted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a strait of sea; 'it' refers back to the sea of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A seascape is a painting of the sea, the 'it' of the surface.

clue.text: Where Welsh may be found chewing bread in most of region

indicators.note: chewing mashes the word up, so its letters get rearranged
most of drops the final letter

parts.note: an area is a region

explanation.surface: Welsh people munching bread across much of the region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chewing' scrambles BREAD to ABERD; 'most of' trims AREA to ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdare is a town in South Wales, so a place to find Welsh people.

clue.text: Band's ring is heard on time

indicators.note: is heard means the word is used for its sound alone

parts.note: a ring is the sound of a bell; BELL said aloud matches BEL

explanation.surface: A band's ring tone can be heard punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: BEL, a unit of loudness, sounds just like BELL.
explanation.definitionFit: A belt is a strip or stripe, as a belt of trees or a band of colour.

clue.text: German queen pursuing composer

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so this piece comes after

parts.note: Irving Berlin was the songwriter of White Christmas
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A German queen chasing a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: A Berliner is a native of Berlin, so a German.

clue.text: Troubled client stopped short to meet landlord

indicators.note: troubled means the letters are disturbed into a new order
stopped short cuts off the last letter

parts.note: to see someone is to meet them

explanation.surface: An upset customer cut off a chat to see the landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopped short' trims CLIENT to CLIEN; 'Troubled' scrambles that to LICEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A licensee holds a licence to sell alcohol, as a British pub landlord does.

clue.text: Liqueur I arrange to be included in stake

indicators.note: to be included in places one piece inside another

parts.note: the ante is the stake put up in poker
to set is to arrange, as in setting a table

explanation.surface: Someone arranges for a liqueur to be part of a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: Anisette is a sweet aniseed-flavoured liqueur.

clue.text: Means devised around Louisiana for communication?

indicators.note: around means one piece encloses the other
devised means the letters are worked out into a new order

parts.note: LA is the postal abbreviation for Louisiana

explanation.surface: Methods invented around Louisiana for talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devised' gives AMESN from the five letters of 'Means'; the question mark flags the definition as an example of communication.
explanation.definitionFit: Ameslan is American Sign Language, a means of communicating by gesture.

clue.text: Stone fish found by nurse

parts.note: the sar or sargo is a sea bream
SEN is a State Enrolled Nurse, a former British nursing grade

explanation.surface: A stonefish discovered by a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone fish' reads as one creature, but Stone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarsens are the large sandstone boulders found in southern England, used at Stonehenge.

clue.text: Recorded fragment about tailless pigeon

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: an end is a leftover piece, as in a fag end

indicators.note: tailless removes the final letter of the word

parts.note: the roller is a breed of tumbling pigeon

explanation.surface: A scrap of tape captured a pigeon with no tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' leaves ROLLE; an end is a remnant, as in a fag end (cigarette stub).
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to enter on a register or record, so enrolled means recorded.

clue.text: Farming method that requires a baler to work

definitions.text: Farming method that requires a baler to work

indicators.note: to work means the letters are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: A type of farming needing a baling machine to operate.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: crop farming is the kind that needs a baler.
explanation.definitionFit: Arable farming grows crops, such as hay and straw, which balers pack up.

clue.text: Scientist making maggot eat cuckoos

indicators.note: eat means one piece swallows the other, holding it inside

parts.note: a bott (bot) is the larva of the botfly
the ani is a tropical American bird of the cuckoo family

explanation.surface: A scientist gets a maggot to feed on cuckoos.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanist is a scientist who studies plants.

clue.text: A long time to find bird in east, it took years at first

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
a tern is a seabird
taken as written

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Spotting a bird in the east took years at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyperbolically, an eternity is a very long wait.

clue.text: A lot of writing on singular set of principles

parts.note: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular
a creed is a set of beliefs or principles

explanation.surface: Lengthy writing based on one particular code of beliefs.
explanation.definitionFit: A screed is a long, often tedious, piece of writing.
